packs.title: Gardens, Coast and Everyday Objects
packs.promise: Explore George Town’s public coast, gardens and everyday heritage, with a separate Air Itam and Penang Hill day trip.

q.s: Collect evidence of everyday life in P. Ramlee’s birthplace.
st: Enter the visitor exhibition during its open session. Build a small evidence card with three headings: storing, dressing and resting.

Find the family safe box used for clothing, a displayed everyday-clothing item, and a bedroom feature. For each heading, record one actual feature or label that explains its domestic use; collect observations, not objects.
Choose the clue that most changes how you picture this home. Explain your choice in one sentence, using the display rather than inventing a story about P. Ramlee.

q.s: Make an original picture from the contrast between tall buildings and a broad public edge.
st: On an open public path, find a lawful stopped view that includes at least one actual tall building and a broad horizontal edge of the promenade, planting or coast.
Create a two-band drawing: give the upper band the skyline’s vertical rhythm and the lower band the long public edge. A short written scene with an upper and lower paragraph works equally well.
Add one observed detail that fixes the work to this real Gurney setting. Keep construction or reclamation as you actually see it rather than replacing it with an imagined beach.

q.s: Let a real public garden path set a comfortable rhythm for movement.
st: At the public entrance, choose an open paved visitor circuit shown on today’s signs. Decide on a short comfortable out-and-back if a loop is unsuitable; there is no distance target.

Walk or roll for about ten minutes at your own easy pace. Stop at a lawful resting point, notice how the garden path turns through its planting, then follow the same open visitor route back or finish the signed circuit.

Record the path turn or planted feature that helped you orient yourself, and the pace that suited you. Rest as needed; you do not have to use stairs, a trail, a tram or a particular length to earn credit.

packs.title: Living Heritage Streets
packs.promise: Explore the connected heritage core through public street views, admitted clan and Mansion visits, and a respectful quay pause.

q.s: Build an original small design from an admitted Mansion visit.
st: Enter on the appropriate admission and follow the current visitor route. Without taking interior photos or video, choose a visible wood, tile or metal detail that catches your attention; find two other actual details to balance it.

After leaving the Mansion, draw a small original arrangement of those three remembered details, or write three short descriptive lines. You can note an uncertain material as uncertain; do not invent an object or historical story.
Give the design a short original caption in your own voice and adjust one shape or word so the details fit together. Describe your actual admitted visit with the work.

q.s: Keep the Yap association and adjacent temple distinct in your observations.
st: Make two headings: association hall and adjacent temple. From the public pavement, locate the green hall and the red temple without entering either.

Collect three paired observations across the two fronts: their roof outlines, their opening shapes, and one visible colour or surface difference. A material you cannot identify may be described as a texture.
Choose the pair that most clearly separates the two buildings and explain it. Keep each feature under the correct heading rather than making a single combined façade.

q.s: Move through a short living street while noticing how its edge changes.
st: Choose the currently open public pedestrian route along the short Armenian Street segment. Begin at an easy pace with no need to visit a shop.

As you walk or roll, stop in two lawful clear spaces to notice how the street edge changes: a shophouse opening, a shaded frontage, or the park-side space. Describe what you actually see without blocking a doorway.
Finish near the Armenian Park side and record one change that affected your pace or attention. A shorter open segment with a turn back works if the full route is unsuitable.
